prompt.title: Design an image from the following information. If a reference image is attached, use it as an overall layout reference.
prompt.regionSemanticsGuidance: - Every region is a zone of visual influence, not a fixed final silhouette. Unless a note explicitly requires it, do not reproduce complete boundaries, outlines, or closed panels.
prompt.displayTextGuidance: - Every text region must contain visible typography. Provided display text must appear exactly; a blank field means the model creates the copy, not that typography may be omitted. Text may be distorted or partially occluded according to its depth and image relationships.
prompt.coordinateOrigin: - Positions are percentages relative to the overall image, with 0%, 0% at the top left.
prompt.referenceValues: - Positions, proportions, and angles describe the visual relationships among the main content.
prompt.flexibleImplementation: - Preserve relative placement, scale hierarchy, visual weight, depth, and visual flow. Reconstruct, split, merge, overlap, or bleed regions as the real content requires.
prompt.referenceImageGuidance: - The uploaded reference image expresses only approximate placement, visual weight, and distribution. It is a spatial cue, not line art; do not reproduce complete boundaries, markers, or lines in the final image.
prompt.occupied: - Main content occupies about {{value}}% of the overall image
prompt.generatedDisplayText: - Copy: Create suitable text, but do not leave this region blank or replace it with ordinary image content
prompt.referencePosition: - Reference position: {{x}}% from the left, {{y}}% from the top
prompt.referenceArea: - Visible content occupies about {{area}}% of the overall image
prompt.referenceClipping: - Content extends beyond the image on the {{sides}}
prompt.lightSourceGuidance: - Like ordinary shape regions, light markers describe approximate visual intent and spatial relationships. Pale yellow identifies lighting, not color temperature. A source is distinct from the area it illuminates: interpret its origin and contribution in the scene. Rectangles suggest band-shaped or extended illumination; circles suggest localized illumination. Retain the broad lighting placement, extension trend and contribution to subject and space, while freely adapting width, length, curvature, continuity, edges and strength to the scene. User instructions and node notes take precedence; otherwise the Agent chooses. Do not infer fixed width, straight constant-width strips, full-frame coverage, medium-strong contrast or thumbnail prominence from the reference. Consider sources individually while allowing their visible effects to split, overlap or blend. Review whether the overall lighting broadly echoes the composition rather than comparing edges, segments or widths; tighten a constraint only when the user explicitly requests it, and do not ignore the authored lighting intent entirely.
prompt.lightBandGuidance: Light-band intent: broadly retain the extended or band-like illumination and its spatial role here. Its realization may narrow, widen, curve, break up or blend with the scene; a complete, straight, constant-width or conspicuous stripe is not required. User instructions and this node’s notes take precedence for width, length, edges and strength; otherwise the Agent interprets them freely. An approximate overall correspondence is sufficient.

mode.label: Mode
mode.unselectedGuidance: - Choose Scene or Editorial before continuing.
mode.sceneGuidance: - Compose every region as part of one scene. Text may follow perspective, distortion, layering, and partial occlusion.
mode.editorialGuidance: - Arrange every region as an editorial layout, balancing hierarchy, alignment, spacing, negative space, reading flow, and focal relationships. Regions are not UI components or fixed panels.

prompt.staticTitle: Design and implement an interface using the following information.
prompt.motionTitle: Design and implement the interface and its state transitions using the following information.
prompt.canvasOrigin: - Use the top-left corner of the canvas as the coordinate origin.
prompt.referenceValues: - The coordinates, dimensions, and font sizes below are reference values that communicate approximate placement, hierarchy, and transition direction.
prompt.perceptibleElementGuidance: - The sketch contains only key elements that users can see, read, recognize, or interact with and their spatial relationships. A rectangle represents a perceptible content footprint or visual surface, not a component-tree node; do not implement layout-only wrappers, stacks, grids, or parent rectangles with no independent visual meaning as containers.
prompt.flexibleImplementation: - Do not reproduce them with rigid fixed positioning or pixel-perfect placement. Adjust them to suit the actual content, component constraints, responsive layout, and visual quality.
prompt.motionStateGuidance: - States transition in tab order. In each transition, the first state describes the baseline appearance; the next state lists only changed properties. Properties not listed remain unchanged.
prompt.motionClosing: Design a natural layout transition from each element's state changes. Treat the reference coordinates as guidance for relative placement and movement, not as rigid fixed positions.

spatial.cameraBoxHint: Six inward orthographic views show only the box interior. Directions rotate with the box. Use the sheet to understand the pose and the main camera for composition.
spatial.cameraBoxViewError: --view must be sheet, front, back, left, right, top, or bottom.
spatial.cameraBoxViewsError: Choose 1–6 distinct directions from front, back, left, right, top, bottom, separated by commas.
spatial.cameraBoxGenerationGuidance: The main camera sets the final composition. The observation sheet shows the same scene at one moment; labels identify box-local directions, not anatomical left and right. Use auxiliary views to understand occlusion, digit ownership, and approximate bending intent. Produce a single image without a contact-sheet layout, duplicated subjects, direction labels, or joint/body guide lines. Correct anatomy and finger contact naturally instead of reproducing the references pixel for pixel.
